title: Raise request draft + evidence log
content:
Goal: build a concise, evidence-based ask for a comp increase and updated role title to present in 1:1 with manager (week of Mar 15).

Summary (one-liner): Over the last 18 months I led the people ops transition for Dedicated hires, drove a faster interview-to-offer cadence, and launched the new leveling rubric; I’m requesting a market-aligned comp adjustment (+12% base) and title bump to Sr. People Ops Partner to reflect scope.

What I own (current scope):
- Core: individual contributor for people ops, embedded with Eng infra (serving-runtime) and Applied ML teams; manage hiring roadmap for two IC-heavy teams.
- Programs: revamped interview loop (reduced panel length), launched new interview scorecard template, ran 6 hiring manager workshops.
- Projects: led compensation band refresh pilot for ICs (pilot group: 24 roles), built pay-equity dashboard with finance for March cadence.
- Mentorship: informal mentor to 3 junior recruiters and 2 rotational HR interns; ran hiring calibration sessions.

Impact + evidence (specific examples):
1) Hiring velocity: reduced avg time-to-offer from 46 -> 31 days for infra roles (Oct 2025 -> Feb 2026). Source: ATS exports; conversion funnel snapshot (attached link in artifacts).
2) Cost avoidance: improved offer acceptance through clearer total comp communication -> decreased second-offer churn from 9% to 3% for mid-SD hires; estimated avoided re-hiring cost ~$32k.
3) Compensation pilot: designed and executed band refresh pilot; presented to comp committee 2026-02-18; pilot has 24 roles and 4 adjustments approved. Material: CON-8234.
4) Cross-functional reliability: when Dedicated capacity rolling outages hit in Dec, I coordinated on-call hiring surge plan and temp contractor process that filled 3 critical gaps in 10 days. Note: SRE and release-eng confirmed reduced incident staffing gaps.
5) Enablement: created the new interview rubric that decreased score variance across panelists (std dev down 22%); sample rubric (link).

Qualitative signals: consistent positive feedback from hiring managers (quotes below), recognition in Q4 all-hands for process improvements, peer note from Jordan praising ownership of the comp project.

Draft ask & rationale: 
- Compensation: +12% base salary adjustment (benchmarked to market and internal parity). Rationale: market data (benchmarks compiled with finance), impact on hiring outcomes, scope expansion (now covering 2 orgs + comp pilot).
- Title: Sr. People Ops Partner (reflecting scope and increased cross-functional influence).
- Timeline: request decision/response by end of March to align with next comp cycle and offers.

BATNA / fallback options: 
- If comp can't move immediately: ask for a mid-cycle spot bonus (one-time) and a commitment to review in Q3 2026 with target uplift.
- If title constrained: ask for official role charter update and public announcement of changed responsibilities + increased ownership (step toward title change).

Manager prep notes (what to say in 1:1):
- Open: "I want to talk about role scope and compensation — I’ve pulled together outcomes and a proposed ask."
- Lead with evidence: 2–3 concrete metrics (time-to-offer drop, acceptance improvement, comp pilot deliverable).
- Emphasize goal alignment: hiring velocity and pay equity improve product timelines and lower costs.
- Ask for explicit next steps and timeline (who else needs to be involved, when will comp committee review?).

Potential objections & responses:
- Objection: "Budget is tight for this quarter." Response: propose split (partial increase now + review later) or spot bonus; show avoided re-hire cost math.
- Objection: "Title inflation across the org." Response: show role charter and comparators; emphasize scope change and cross-functional work (comp committee, hiring playbooks).

Open questions / things to collect before meeting:
- Latest market comp bands for Sr. People Ops Partner comparator (ask finance for updated 2026-03 comp file).
- ATS export for offer timeline (ask recruiting ops to pull weekly buckets for last 12 months).
- Specific quotes from 2 hiring managers to drop into the note (ask Jordan & Priya).
- Confirmation of headcount savings / avoided cost calculation from finance.

Notes-to-self / rehearsal phrases (short):
- "I enjoy the work and want to keep scaling impact — I’d like my compensation and title to reflect that contribution."
- "I want clarity: timeline and decision-owner. If we can’t decide this month, what’s milestone for a Q3 review?"

Misc scribbles / rough evidence snippets (copy-paste from emails):
- "Ravi, the new rubric made calibrations so much easier. We moved from 3 rounds of interviews to 2 for the recent infra hires." — Priya (hiring manager), 2026-02-11
- "He ran the comp pilot with great detail and surfaced pay gaps we missed earlier." — Finance lead, 2026-02-20

Action checklist (before 1:1):
- [ ] Pull comp benchmark file (finance).
- [ ] Attach ATS funnel export and charts.
- [ ] Collect 2 manager quotes.
- [ ] Draft short email to manager with one-line ask + doc link.
- [ ] Rehearse 5-minute talking points.

Version history / previous asks: 
- Feb 2025: informal ask for market adjustment — deferred due to freeze.
- Nov 2025: performance sync where manager acknowledged expanded scope and suggested we revisit at next comp cycle.

Tone notes: keep concise, factual, non-entitled. Avoid long personal narratives; focus on team impact and measurable outcomes.

---
Scratch area (brainstorm):
- Would a peer-calibration session with other Sr POPs help justify title? Rapid idea: table with responsibilities vs comparators.
- Could a small internal spotlight (All-hands 1-slide) increase visibility for these improvements and support faster approval?
- If denied, plan for next 6 months: take on 2 high-impact hiring projects and formalize mentorship program to justify raise.

End of draft.

(Notes: this is a working doc — edit freely. Keep final email short: 2 lines ask + link to evidence.)
